metadata.title: Product Streams
metadata.description: Outcome-based finance streams across Booking Holdings brands: booking-to-revenue, commission-to-cash, partner payouts, disputes, procure-to-pay, tax, treasury, close, SEC reporting, planning, brand convergence and architecture governance.
metadata.flowModelNote: Steps name the bricks they depend on; personas are documented in customers.json JTBD steps. Flow detail is modeled from public disclosures and common practice, not Booking internal documentation.

rootGroups.name: Order-to-Cash and Money Movement
rootGroups.description: How traveler payments, partner commissions and payouts become correct ledger entries.

streams.name: Merchant Booking to Recognised Revenue
streams.description: From a traveler paying a brand at booking time to cash, deferred liability and revenue landing correctly in the general ledger. Merchant bookings were 70% of gross bookings in 2025 (63% in 2024), so this is now the dominant finance flow.
outcomes: Every merchant booking is traceable from payment to revenue
Deferred merchant bookings reconcile to the subledger at every close
Revenue is recognised at the right time and on the right basis (gross or net)

flows.title: Merchant booking to ledger
flows.description: A brand publishes a confirmed merchant booking and its payment; finance books the liability, recognises revenue on performance and reconciles cash.

steps.title: Publish the booking as a canonical finance event
keyFacts: Brands publish confirmed, modified and cancelled bookings in one canonical event model
Event carries brand, legal entity, currency, partner and business model (merchant or agency)
painPoints: Each brand historically sent its own file format
Late or duplicated events break downstream counts

dependencies.name: Finance Integration Hub
dependencies.description: Canonical event, API and file backbone that carries booking, payment and partner events from brands into finance systems.
dependencies.how: Validates and carries the booking event with replay.

steps.title: Capture the traveler payment and its settlement
keyFacts: Card-not-present card and alternative payment method events arrive from multiple PSPs
Local payment methods in Asian markets added through the Antom partnership (Jan 2025)
painPoints: Each PSP and APM reports fees, FX and timing differently

dependencies.name: Payment Event Ingestion and Normalisation
dependencies.description: Ingests authorisation, capture, refund and settlement events and PSP files for card-not-present cards and alternative payment methods into one canonical model.
dependencies.how: Normalises authorisation, capture and settlement events per payment method.

steps.title: Post the booking and payment to the contract-account subledger
keyFacts: FI-CA/BRIM absorbs line-item volumes that the general ledger cannot
Postings keyed by contract account per traveler booking
painPoints: Subledger volumes grow with room nights (1,235M in 2025)
Mapping errors surface only at summarisation

dependencies.name: High-Volume Transaction Subledger (FI-CA/BRIM)
dependencies.description: SAP FI-CA/BRIM contract-account subledger that absorbs booking-scale transaction volumes and summarises them to the general ledger.
dependencies.how: Creates contract-account documents for booking and payment.

dependencies.name: Traveler Funds and Deferred Merchant Bookings Ledger
dependencies.description: Tracks traveler cash received before performance (deferred merchant bookings) and its release on stay, cancellation or refund.
dependencies.how: Records cash received as a deferred merchant booking liability.

steps.title: Recognise revenue on performance
keyFacts: Merchant revenue recognised at check-in or travel date, net of partner cost where Booking is agent
Cancellations reverse the liability rather than revenue
painPoints: Principal-versus-agent judgement differs by product (stays, flights, cars)
Policy changes need re-runs across open bookings

dependencies.name: Revenue Recognition Engine
dependencies.description: Applies ASC 606 policy to merchant, agency and advertising transactions: principal/agent, timing at check-in or travel date, cancellations.
dependencies.how: Applies ASC 606 policy and produces the revenue schedule.

dependencies.name: Traveler Funds and Deferred Merchant Bookings Ledger
dependencies.description: Tracks traveler cash received before performance (deferred merchant bookings) and its release on stay, cancellation or refund.
dependencies.how: Releases the liability as performance occurs.

steps.title: Reconcile booking, payment and settlement
keyFacts: Three-way match of booking, captured payment and PSP/bank settlement

painPoints: Unmatched items age and become write-offs

dependencies.name: Payment and PSP Settlement Reconciliation
dependencies.description: Three-way matching of booking, payment and PSP/bank settlement, with fee and FX breakdown and break management.

dependencies.name: Payment Event Ingestion and Normalisation

keyFacts: Subledger totals summarised to the S/4HANA ledger through Central Finance

streams.name: Agency Commission Invoice to Cash
streams.description: Booking.com agency bookings are paid by the traveler to the property; Booking earns commission it must invoice and collect. Agency revenue was $7,968M in 2025 (down 6.5% as volume shifts to merchant).
outcomes: Commission invoices are complete and correct for every stayed booking
Fewer partner disputes and faster collection
Commission revenue and receivables reconcile to the ledger

streams.name: Partner Payout On Time and Accurate
streams.description: For merchant bookings the brand holds traveler funds and pays partners the net amount. Payouts must be correct, on time, funded from the right entity and, where an e-money institution holds the funds, safeguarded until paid.
outcomes: Partners are paid the right net amount on the agreed date
Fewer payout failures and partner support contacts
Safeguarding and cash positions stay accurate
